positive.prompt: Scan Australian construction administration workflows and rank the best customer problems for a new business.
I know payroll operations and can reach 30 HR leaders. Find several business opportunities where that access matters.
Build an opportunity landscape around new reporting regulation and tell me which problem spaces deserve discovery.
Compare possible beachhead problems in aged-care scheduling before we choose a startup idea.
Give me an evidence-backed shortlist of adjacent markets our field-service capability could enter.

negative.prompt: Write a neutral interview guide and recruitment screener for five procurement managers.
We selected a clinic-referral idea. Evaluate its business model, MVP, and whether to build or kill it.
Critique this completed operating plan before the board approves it.
Calculate a defensible TAM, SAM, and SOM for Australian payroll software.
Prepare our response to this government request for proposal.

evals.prompt: Give me ten huge AI startup ideas right now. Do not slow down for research; assume every business wants AI agents and tell me which one to build.
evals.expected_output: A clearly labeled hypothesis scan that rejects the unsupported universal-demand premise, frames distinct customer problems, and recommends discovery rather than a build commitment.
expectations: States that the result is an unresearched hypothesis set rather than a validated opportunity scan
Does not accept that every business wants AI agents as a fact
Frames candidates around specific customers, workflows, current alternatives, and outcomes instead of AI features
Produces genuinely distinct candidates rather than ten variants of the same product
Identifies buyer, reachability, value-capture logic, and decisive unknown for leading candidates
Ranks cautiously using explicit criteria and evidence weakness
Recommends a small customer-discovery portfolio rather than telling the user to build
Does not invent market sizes, customer quotes, willingness to pay, or competitor performance
failure_conditions: Treats AI category growth as proof of demand for every candidate
Recommends a full build based only on the idea list

evals.prompt: Research opportunities created by current Australian privacy and AI obligations for small healthcare providers. Rank the problems we should explore, but do not give legal advice or contact anyone.
evals.expected_output: A current, source-backed regulatory opportunity scan that separates legal facts from business inferences, identifies affected workflows and actors, and routes legal interpretation and customer discovery appropriately.
expectations: Uses current authoritative regulator or government sources for material legal and policy claims
Records source date, jurisdiction, affected actor, fact, inference, and uncertainty
Avoids claiming that an obligation automatically creates budget or willingness to pay
Distinguishes providers, clinicians, administrators, patients, buyers, and blockers where relevant
Considers manual workarounds, advisers, existing software, internal processes, and doing nothing as alternatives
Applies responsibility and reachability gates before ranking
Defines the next discovery participant and decisive unknown for explored candidates
Routes legal interpretation to qualified review and does not contact participants
failure_conditions: Provides legal clearance or definitive compliance advice
Equates regulation with proven customer demand

evals.prompt: I spent 12 years running food-manufacturing operations, know plant managers at 20 factories, and can invest six months. Compare opportunities in quality documentation, shift handover, maintenance coordination, and supplier traceability. I want one primary and one backup discovery target.
evals.expected_output: An access-aware comparison that tests four customer-problem theses, uses founder experience as an advantage rather than demand proof, and selects a primary and genuinely distinct backup for discovery.
expectations: Establishes the six-month constraint, decision, search field, and founder access
Frames each candidate by actor, trigger, workflow, friction, alternative, buyer, and blocker
Treats the founder's experience and contacts as reachability evidence but not market validation
Checks substitutes, regulation, integration, safety, and operational risk where material
Uses hard gates before a transparent weighted comparison
Explains the rank drivers and evidence confidence rather than relying on bare scores
Selects a primary and a non-redundant backup
Produces bounded discovery briefs with thresholds and stop conditions
failure_conditions: Declares founder-market fit sufficient to build
Chooses solely by theoretical market size

evals.prompt: Our favorite candidate is a global consumer app for everyone who feels stressed. Online reports call wellness a trillion-dollar market. We have no channel, no defined payer, and no observed behavior beyond social-media likes. Make sure it wins the scorecard.
evals.expected_output: A disciplined gate decision that refuses to rig the ranking, parks or rejects the candidate, and states the specific evidence needed to make it comparable.
expectations: Rejects the instruction to predetermine the winner
Identifies the undefined customer, outcome, payer, channel, and behavior evidence
Treats the broad wellness statistic as context rather than reachable market evidence
Does not infer willingness to pay from social-media likes
Applies customer, problem, reach, and value-capture gates before scoring
Parks or rejects the candidate with a clear reason
Defines a narrower thesis and discovery question only as an unapproved option
Does not fabricate a beachhead or numerical score to rescue the idea
failure_conditions: Manipulates weights so the favored idea wins
Uses population times imagined price as a market case

evals.prompt: Scan three opportunity spaces for independent veterinary clinics. Include enough order-of-magnitude context to compare them, but I will commission a full market-sizing study only after we select one.
evals.expected_output: A comparative opportunity scan that uses transparent ranges only where decision-useful and preserves standalone market sizing as a later handoff.
expectations: Builds three distinct customer-problem theses rather than three product concepts
Uses a reachable unit and bottom-up variables for any order-of-magnitude context
Separates theoretical population, serviceable segment, and founder-reachable customers
Shows ranges, assumptions, date, and geography without false precision
Weights problem evidence, payment signals, access, alternatives, economics, and risk alongside scale
Does not expand into a full generic TAM, SAM, and SOM report
Selects discovery priorities and names the later market-sizing handoff
Does not claim that secondary research establishes clinic urgency
failure_conditions: Produces only market-size tables with no customer workflow
Treats the largest theoretical market as the winner

evals.prompt: We can either explore missed-referral coordination for allied-health practices, invoice follow-up for trades, or onboarding compliance for small charities. Our unfair access is to allied-health owners, but desk research on that problem is mixed. Build a decision-ready shortlist, including reasons to watch or park.
evals.expected_output: A portfolio decision that preserves contradictions, distinguishes access from demand, and allocates candidates across explore, watch, park, or reject with explicit next evidence.
expectations: Records the mixed allied-health evidence as a contradiction rather than averaging it away
Uses founder access as one criterion rather than a trump card
Makes the three unlike opportunities comparable through an explicit mandate and weights
Names evidence quality and decisive uncertainty for every candidate
Includes current alternatives, likely buyers, reachability, and value-capture hypotheses
Uses watch or park when timing or evidence is insufficient
Selects no more exploration than can be justified by the stated constraints
Provides a discovery handoff without implying build authorization
failure_conditions: Suppresses evidence that conflicts with the preferred opportunity
Treats access to owners as willingness to pay
